overall_reason: The ops table is sound (right-aligned monospaced amounts, deltas with arrows as well as colour, status with icon and word), but the three tiles above it carry no period or comparison while a '7 days' range control sits under them.

score.reason: T-SECOND-ENCODING and T-FIGURES pass on the urgent table; T-STAT-TILE fails on the three headline tiles and on the unexplained 'Change' column (DVZ-013).

findings.where: main > section.stats > div.stat (three tiles), 1440 and 375, contact sheet #1 to #3, tiles/1440-00.png
findings.evidence: The tiles read 'Open threads 128', 'Waiting on us 14' and 'Pipeline $42.6k' (stat_tiles, 28px). None names a period or a comparison. The Range control directly below them has '7 days' selected, so the reader cannot tell whether the tiles follow it.
findings.before: Three figures with a label and no period, delta or baseline.
findings.after: Put the period in each tile and a comparison under it, for example 'Open threads, last 7 days: 128' with '+9 on the previous 7 days' and an arrow.
findings.why: On an operations screen the first question is whether a number is getting better or worse; a figure with no period or comparison cannot answer it.

findings.evidence: The column shows '↘ 12%' in red for Harbor and Co, '↗ 4%' and '↗ 1%' in green. The header says only 'Change': it does not say which value changed (the amount, the reply time) or over what period.
findings.before: A change column with no named measure or baseline.
findings.after: Name the measure and period in the header, for example 'Amount vs last week'.
findings.why: A reader cannot act on a 12% drop without knowing what dropped and since when.

strengths: The Urgent table right-aligns its amounts ('$18,400', '$6,200', '$1,050') in a monospaced face, so the columns line up.
Deltas carry an arrow as well as red or green, and each status pairs an icon and a word with its colour ('Blocked', 'Waiting', 'Clear'), so the table reads in grayscale and for colour-blind readers.
The screen keeps to tiles and one table: no decorative chart.
